summary: Regression pass after api.ts + chat.tsx edits (real error surfacing, 60s AbortController timeout, filename sanitization, missing-BASE guard). Backend: 18/18 pytest tests PASSED against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL, including 3 NEW media tests: (a) multipart PNG upload -> POST /api/messages/media returns media message, appears in /api/messages and /api/gallery, bytes round-trip via GET /api/files/{path} both with X-User-Id header AND ?uid= query; (b) one_time privacy flow: recipient blocked 403 before open, sender blocked 410, open works once then 410 on retry, item excluded from /gallery; (c) unauthenticated /messages/media -> 401. Frontend UI (mobile viewport 390x844): app boots without red screen, onboarding create-space -> tabs works, /chat loads, POST /api/messages/text sends and renders (`REGRESSION_hello_...` visible), attach sheet opens (testID attach-btn) and all 7 sub-testIDs render (privacy-none / privacy-no_save / privacy-one_time / capture-photo / capture-video / pick-photo / pick-video), privacy-one_time toggle does not crash. Zero real console errors during the flow (the only noise is the pre-existing 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' warning from a third-party lib). No new import/runtime breakage introduced by the api.ts edit. Native camera/gallery pick itself is not exercisable on react-native-web, per the request.

react_native_issues.issue: Non-blocking console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Pre-existing from iteration_1, unrelated to this change set.

action_items: No blocking action items. The frontend edits to /app/frontend/src/api.ts (AbortController + timeout, sanitized filename, BASE guard) and /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/chat.tsx (surfacing e.message via toast) are safe: no regressions to text send, chat UI, attach sheet, or media endpoints.

The reported 'could not send media' from the built APK cannot be reproduced from the web preview (native ImagePicker unavailable on web). Diagnosis must continue on-device using the newly surfaced e.message text in the toast.
critical_code_review_comments: api.ts uploadMedia: FormData construction is correct for both web (Blob) and native ({uri,name,type}); Content-Type is intentionally NOT set on the fetch so multipart boundary is generated by the runtime — good.
60000ms AbortController timeout is reasonable for a 25MB cap; on Android with slow LTE a >60s upload will now surface 'Upload timed out. Check your connection and try again.' — clear message.
Filename fallback sanitizes query/hash and guarantees an extension (photo.jpg / video.mp4). Backend already re-derives extension anyway (server.py:353-355), so this is defense-in-depth.
server.py is ~620 lines; still fine but splitting into routers/services would help long-term.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_2gether_flows.py (added TestMedia with 3 cases + tiny in-memory PNG helper; fixed default BASE_URL fallback to current preview host)
seed_data_creation: TEST_Alex/TEST_Sam couple + TEST_Chat_<ts> user created via public API/UI. Media objects uploaded to Emergent object storage under get2gether/uploads/<user_id>/. Preview DB is isolated; not cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend tests with: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_2gether_flows.py -v. Default fallback URL now matches current .env. UI testIDs on chat screen: attach-btn, chat-input, send-btn, privacy-none/no_save/one_time, capture-photo, capture-video, pick-photo, pick-video, uploading-indicator, media-<id>, media-onetime-<id>. Native ImagePicker cannot be triggered on react-native-web; use pytest for /messages/media coverage.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug fix run — this iteration is a regression check of the frontend hardening in api.ts (AbortController + timeout + filename sanitization + BASE guard) and chat.tsx (surfacing the real error message via toast.show(e?.message)). All server-side media paths remain unchanged and continue to work end-to-end. The user's APK-only 'could not send media' will now show the concrete failure reason on-device (network error / timeout / server detail), which is the intended diagnostic step.
